question: According to the European Court of Auditors’ analysis of 1 January 2024, the situation in the EU regarding traineeships is improving with an increase in the number of trainees. However, the report also highlights significant problems, particularly as regards the youth unemployment rate, which, although decreasing, was above 11 % in 2022, almost twice as high as the EU average, which lay at 6.2 %.

In view of the above: What curricular and extracurricular measures does the Commission intend to take to improve matters in the field of traineeships and to enhance the employment prospects for young Europeans?
answer: EN On behalf of the European Commission (9.4.2024) Quality traineeships can play a key role in helping young people gain work experience and find a job. A majority of young Europeans (68%) participating in a recent Eurobarometer survey1 were employed and 18% continued their studies six months after their last traineeship.

However, there is a need to improve the use, quality of and access to traineeships across the EU, so that they provide a genuine learning and work experience facilitating education-towork and job-to-job transitions, also for groups in vulnerable situations. On 20 March 2024, the Commission adopted proposals for a Directive and for a Council Recommendation on this matter.

They aim at improving working conditions for trainees and combatting regular employment relationships disguised as traineeships, as well as ensuring that traineeships really help young people access regular work after the traineeship.

The Commission supports the acquisition of skills and experience abroad that increase the employability of young people through programmes such as Erasmus+, the European Social Fund Plus and the European Solidarity Corps. For example, the Erasmus+ programme co-finances traineeships abroad for university students and vocational education and training learners.

In order to make such mobility a quality experience, fully integrated in educational systems and accessible to all young people, the Commission adopted a proposal for a Council Recommendation ‘Europe on the Move’ – learning mobility opportunities for everyone2 on 15 November 2023.
1 https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/surveys/detail/2964 2 Europe on the Move - a proposal on the future of learning mobility, European Education Area
